rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose verb for scheduling when something happens or how long it lasts.

example.english: We need to arrange a time for the meeting.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 jiu3 on1 paai4 si4 gaan3 hoi1 wui6

rows.note: Use this when the emphasis is on choosing a suitable moment for an event or action.

example.english: You need to choose the right time before talking to him.
example.traditional: 你要揀啱時間先好同佢講。
example.jyutping: nei5 jiu3 gaan2 ngaam1 si4 gaan3 sin1 hou2 tung4 keoi5 gong2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for time as an abstract flow, available duration, or measured length.

example.english: The time really goes by quickly.
example.jyutping: si4 gaan3 zan1 hai6 gwo3 dak1 hou2 faai3

rows.note: Use this when measuring or recording duration or running time, such as with a stopwatch.

example.english: I use my phone to time how long the run takes.
example.traditional: 我用手機計時，睇下跑步要幾耐。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jung6 sau2 gei1 gai3 si4 tai2 haa5 paau2 bou6 jiu3 gei2 noi6

rows.note: Use this for a numerical clock time, especially when asking or stating what time it is.

example.english: Do you know what time it is now?
example.jyutping: nei5 zi1 m4 zi1 ji4 gaa1 gei2 dim2

rows.note: Use this for the appropriate moment or occasion when something should happen, rather than for a clock reading.

example.english: It’s so late now; it’s time to go to bed.
example.traditional: 而家都咁夜，係時候瞓覺喇。
example.jyutping: ji4 gaa1 dou1 gam3 je6 hai6 si4 hau6 fan3 gaau3 laa3

rows.note: Use this for one occurrence or instance, as in 一次 or 再一次, rather than for duration.

example.english: The first time I went to Japan, I joined a tour.
example.traditional: 我第一次去日本係跟團。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dai6 jat1 ci3 heoi3 jat6 bun2 hai6 gan1 tyun4
